styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's density facts are fine: 17 visible tones per tile matches the cheese stall and well, and near-flat coverage is 11%, close to the stall's 13%. The problem is structure. 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so it has a uniform black sticker outline around the whole body. The references use tinted, material-toned edges (hedge 0%, stall 1%, well 33%). Only the lamp is also 100% neutral, and it is a thin object. The blue body has only about 3-4 lightness steps (a light edge, mid blue, dark blue). The window, panel and button areas are mostly flat blocks with little grain or per-element shading. Next to the stall and well, it reads as a clean but flatter, outlined icon, not Beodeul-style selective outlining with ramped shading.

The glass panel and the buttons add some detail, but the large blue casing is mostly smooth with little grain or texture dots. answer.evidence: Rows 0-30 are a flat 28px-wide silhouette. At the top, rows 1-3 are a blue band (L 66 then 122). Row 4 is a very light 1-row line (#e0f2fe), and rows 5-6 are darker blue (L 66), which is consistent with an eave shadow. That fits evidence (a) as a shallow top band of about 3 rows. It could also be a front-facing header sign, so this reading is borderline. Below it, rows 5-30 are a vertical front face with a lit product window (rows 7-19), a dark panel and a lower slot. There is no side face and no ellipse. The kind is a poor match: a vending machine is closer to a machine or appliance than to a bookshelf or cabinet, though it is tall and stands against a wall.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's visible tones per tile (17) match the cheese stall (17) and sit just under the well (20), and its near-flat coverage (11%) is close to the stall's 13%, so density alone would not fail it. The problem is the outline: 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, the same as the crook lamp, while the material-toned references such as the hedge (0%) and the stall (1%) are tinted. The machine reads as a dark navy-black line around every shape, which is the 'sticker' look. The body, glass panel and product rows are mostly 2-3 flat steps each, with little grain, highlight clustering or per-item shading. Beodeul props carry 5-6 steps per material and tinted dark-tone edges, so a careful artist would not accept it beside them without reworking the outline and ramps.

The remaining rows 6-29 are vertical faces: the glass window, the side panel, the tray slot and the base. So the top is 0-2 rows at most, and the front face is large.

styleAnswer.evidence: The vending machine is a blue box with a dark, almost colourless outline all round. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 100%, against 0-44% on the wood, hedge, cheese-stall and well references, so this is the sticker look rather than dark material tone. The blue body shows only about 3 lightness steps (light blue, mid blue, dark blue) against the 5-6 steps of the references. The lit panel and the product window add some detail, but the body, sides and top are mostly flat panels. Visible tones per tile (17) match the cheese stall (17) and are close to the well (20), and near-flat coverage (11%) is similar to the cheese stall's 13%, so density is not far off. The weak points are the neutral outline and the shallow ramps, with little grain, speckle or per-surface texture such as the references have on wood, tile or stone. A careful artist would see it as flatter and more sticker-like next to the references.
